'''Robert Michael Archibald''' (29 March 1980 – 23 January 2020) was a Scottish professional [[basketball]] player. A [[power forward]] or [[Center (basketball)|center]] nicknamed "'''The Flying Scotsman'''" and billed at {{height|ft=6|in=11}}, he was drafted 32nd overall by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] in [[2002 NBA draft|2002]].<ref name="BBC 25 January 2020">{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/basketball/51248659| title= Robert Archibald: Former GB and Scotland basketball player dies at 39| website= [[BBC News Online]]| date= 25 January 2020| access-date= 25 January 2020 }}</ref>

==Early life and high school==
Archibald was born in [[Paisley, Renfrewshire]] and raised in [[Kirkliston]], then [[Dunfermline]]. His father Robert Sr., or Bobby, played for [[Livingston (basketball)|Murray BC]] in Scotland and was capped over 90 times for the Scotland and Great Britain national teams.<ref name="Scot's pair">[http://www.basketballscotland.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=1117&Itemid=387 Scot's pair Make GB Euro Basket Cut]{{dead link|date=April 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Robert himself did not pick up a ball in earnest until he was 14. Afterwards, he began his career at local side [[Dunfermline Reign]], playing at under-16, under-18 and under-21 levels concurrently. By his mid-teens, he was also representing Scotland at junior level before moving to the U.S. in September 1997 and graduating from [[Lafayette High School (Wildwood, Missouri)|Lafayette High School]] in 1998 alongside [[MLB]] player [[Ryan Howard]].

==College career==
In summer 1998, Archibald committed to the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]]. He played 32 games, starting 8, and averaged almost 15 minutes per game as a freshman, while his sophomore year ended with 30 appearances, among them 20 starts.

In his junior year, Archibald started only two games, yet averaged more minutes, points, rebounds and blocks than the previous season. Then, as a senior, he started in almost every game and again increased his output across the board, averaging double digits in scoring and added 5+ rebounds per game in only 22 minutes to help the Fighting Illini to a [[Sweet 16]] appearance. He also collected more fouls than any other player in the [[Big Ten]] that year. Under [[Bill Self]], Illinois won the Big Ten Conference in both Archibald's junior and senior years.

==Professional career==
===NBA===
In 2002, Robert was drafted by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], selected in the second round of the [[NBA Draft]], the third pick of the round, 32nd overall, becoming the first, and to this day the only, Scotsman to play in the NBA. 

After drafting him in the second round, the Grizzlies signed Archibald to a 2-year contract. After one season with the team, in which he played only 12 games, Archibald was traded with [[Brevin Knight]] and [[Cezary Trybański]] to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Bo Outlaw]] and [[Jake Tsakalidis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?id=1627599|title=Suns acquire Knight, Archibald, Trybanski in Memphis trade|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>
On 26 December 2003 Archibald was traded again, this time to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/166053/Suns-Trade-Archibald-to-Orlando|title=Suns Trade Archibald to Orlando - RealGM Wiretap}}</ref> A week later he was traded, for the third time that season, to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Mengke Bateer]] and [[Remon van de Hare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/166200/Raptors-trade-Bateer-to-Orlando-for-Archibald|title=Raptors trade Bateer to Orlando for Archibald - RealGM Wiretap}}</ref> He played 30 games with the Raptors. Archibald's final NBA game was on April 9, 2004, in a 66–74 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]] where he recorded four rebounds but no points. He holds NBA career averages of 1.2 points and 1.6 rebounds per game. <ref name="Guardian 25 Jan" />

===Europe===
Archibald played four seasons in the [[Euroleague]] with [[Scavolini Pesaro]], [[Joventut Badalona]] and two seasons with [[Unicaja Málaga]].<ref name="Unicaja adds">{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/33515/180|title=Unicaja adds size with Robert Archibald|work=Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|date=31 August 2023 }}</ref> 
In July 2011 he signed a one-year contract with [[CAI Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/29341/cai_adds_size_with_robert_archibald.html|title=CAI, firmato Robert Archibald|date=9 July 2011|work=Sportando}}</ref>
Archibald retired after the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in which he represented [[Great Britain men's national basketball team|Great Britain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mvp247.com/2012/05/robert-archibald-retire/|title=Robert Archibald will retire after London 2012|date=15 May 2012|work=MVP|access-date=27 January 2025|archive-date=1 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001064121/https://www.mvp247.com/2012/05/robert-archibald-retire/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===International===
Archibald represented the [[Scotland national basketball team|Scottish national basketball team]] at junior level. He joined the [[Great Britain national basketball team|Great Britain national team]] as it formed in 2007. He represented Great Britain 46 times<ref>{{cite web| last= Hay| first= Katharine| url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/our-hearts-are-broken-tributes-pour-in-for-scottish-nba-robert-archibald-who-died-at-39-1-5080684| title= 'Our hearts are broken': Tributes pour in for Scottish NBA Robert Archibald who died aged 39| date= 25 January 2020|work= [[The Scotsman]]| access-date= 26 January 2020}}</ref> including [[EuroBasket 2009]], [[EuroBasket 2011]], and at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web| last= Riordan| first= Conor| url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/news/glasgow-news/robert-archibald-nba-basketball-paisley-17630610| title= Tributes as Paisley man and NBA star Robert Archibald dies aged 39| date= 25 January 2020| work= GlasgowLive| access-date= 26 January 2020}}</ref>

==Death==
Archibald died of [[suicide by gunshot]] at age 39 at his home in Barrington, Illinois.<ref name="smos">{{cite news|url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-scottish-mail-on-sunday/20200517/282948157419532|date=2020-05-17|author=Mark Woods|publisher=Scottish Mail|archive-url=https://archive.today/20251122033433/https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-scottish-mail-on-sunday/20200517/282948157419532|archive-date=2025-11-22|title=It was a tragedy, the toughest call you can ever take}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Woods |first=Mark |date=January 24, 2020 |title=ROBERT ARCHIBALD DIES, AGED 39 |url=https://www.mvp247.com/2020/01/rip-rob-archibald/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419163826/https://www.mvp247.com/2020/01/rip-rob-archibald/ |archive-date=April 19, 2021 |website=mvp247.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/opinion/18240036.obituary-robert-archibald-basketball-star-scot-play-nba/| title= Obituary: Robert Archibald, basketball star who was the only Scot to play in the NBA| date= 16 February 2020| work= HeraldScotland}}</ref> According to his father, he suffered from depression and was going through a protracted divorce.<ref name="smos"/>
